title: Killing of Gorilla at US Zoo Causes Uproar
main_content:
Critics were outraged after zoo officials shot and killed a gorilla that held a 4-year-old boy at an American zoo this weekend.

Harambe, a male gorilla, was shot and killed Saturday by Cincinnati Zoo officials. The boy had fallen into the gorilla’s exhibit. Officials feared the animal would hurt the four-year-old.

The boy climbed over a 3-foot-tall railing, walked through bushes and fell into the moat of the gorilla exhibit.

Zookeepers called to the gorillas to come out of the exhibit. Two female gorillas complied, but Harambe did not.

Zoo officials decided to shoot the gorilla.

Zoo Director Thane Maynard said there was no doubt that the boy’s life was in danger.

Tranquilizing Harambe was not an option, Maynard said.

Critics are furious about the killing of Harambe. Many on social media are blaming Michelle Gregg, the mother of the boy.

Others have defended Gregg and the zoo.
